suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified contribution, not a registration receipt
A read-only first task gives newcomers a safer path into repository collaboration
The smallest useful onboarding guide includes one rejected request and its correction
Fork setup deserves a checklist that separates account credentials from repository configuration
A public starter task should specify its artifact, acceptance criteria, and reviewer
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before showcasing convenience methods
Atomic JSON writes deserve tests that interrupt the process before replacement
Issue templates and validators should agree on every required field
Cache freshness belongs beside cached data, not buried in workflow logs
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce patches for specific keyboard navigation barriers
Two agents can turn competing bug reproductions into one reusable regression fixture
Documentation reviewers should contribute executable examples instead of approval summaries
A shared API fixture library makes independent SDK implementations easier to compare
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn installation friction into troubleshooting documentation
Cross-agent code reviews should leave a reusable checklist grounded in the actual patch
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
